objective: Inventory existing request/audit/correlation identifiers and map gaps without creating a second tracing store.

existingIdentifiers.name: governedSessionId
existingIdentifiers.purpose: Primary session-level correlation across all governed operations — sessions, tasks, locks, checkpoints, events, scoped writes
existingIdentifiers.propagationPath: transport → session open → all session-scoped operations → event journal → checkpoint → close

existingIdentifiers.name: eventId
existingIdentifiers.purpose: Unique identifier per operational event in the Event Journal; auto-generated on append

existingIdentifiers.name: transportSessionId
existingIdentifiers.purpose: MCP-level transport session identity, binding transport ↔ governed session; REDACTED in logs
existingIdentifiers.propagationPath: HTTP header mcp-session-id → transport map → governed session binding → lock ownership

existingIdentifiers.name: connectionContextId
existingIdentifiers.purpose: Identity of a specific connection context within a governed session (OAuth principal + client + assurance)
existingIdentifiers.propagationPath: session open/resume → connectionContext → attestation validation → session adapter reference

existingIdentifiers.name: taskId
existingIdentifiers.purpose: Task-level correlation for governed task lifecycle (discovered→claimed→transitioning→completed)
existingIdentifiers.propagationPath: task discovery → claim → transitions → checkpoint → terminal chain → done

existingIdentifiers.name: bootstrapReceiptId
existingIdentifiers.purpose: Links session bootstrap to its acknowledged state version, used in terminal verification chain
existingIdentifiers.propagationPath: session acknowledge → receipt → terminal chain verification

existingIdentifiers.name: lockId
existingIdentifiers.purpose: Unique lock identifier for governed locks (scope-bound, session-owned)
existingIdentifiers.propagationPath: lock acquire → renew/conflict/release → event journal → terminal lock release

existingIdentifiers.name: checkpointId
existingIdentifiers.purpose: Unique checkpoint identity capturing session state at a point in time
existingIdentifiers.propagationPath: session checkpoint creation → event journal → audit → terminal checkpoint

existingIdentifiers.name: attestationId
existingIdentifiers.purpose: Tool surface attestation and deploy attestation identity
existingIdentifiers.propagationPath: attestation creation → event journal → deploy verification

existingIdentifiers.name: requestId (GitHub readonly evidence / stablecoin fast-forward)
existingIdentifiers.purpose: Caller-supplied request correlation for GitHub Actions OIDC bounded-write requests
existingIdentifiers.propagationPath: HTTP request body → response echo; NOT propagated to Event Journal or governed session

existingIdentifiers.name: x-github-request-id (GitHub API)
existingIdentifiers.purpose: GitHub API response header captured for diagnostics; not propagated internally
existingIdentifiers.propagationPath: GitHub API response header → diagnostic probe result → log output only

existingIdentifiers.name: principalId / clientId (RequestIdentity)
existingIdentifiers.purpose: Identity correlation — who initiated the request (OAuth subject, client)
existingIdentifiers.propagationPath: auth middleware → RequestIdentity → session open → connectionContext → audit

existingIdentifiers.name: processSequence (Event Journal)
existingIdentifiers.purpose: In-process ordering of events; monotonically incrementing within a single server process
existingIdentifiers.propagationPath: local to event journal; resets on process restart

existingIdentifiers.name: stateVersion
existingIdentifiers.purpose: Versioned global state counter; used for optimistic concurrency across reconciliation and scoped writes
existingIdentifiers.propagationPath: context read → session acknowledge → scoped write gate → terminal chain

existingIdentifiers.name: registryDigest / catalogueDigest / governanceDigest
existingIdentifiers.purpose: Content-addressable digests for registry and governance artefact integrity
existingIdentifiers.propagationPath: bootstrap acknowledge → receipt → event journal metadata

auditPoints.description: Core event journal — appends OperationalEvent with auto-generated eventId, processSequence, occurredAt. All other audit flows funnel through this.
Higher-level audit facade over the event journal; maps structured audit inputs (session, task, lock, checkpoint events) to event journal entries with validated metadata.
Session lifecycle: open, resume, heartbeat, pause, close, checkpoint, bootstrap acknowledge. Each operation audited via OperationalAudit.
Lock lifecycle: acquire, renew, release, expire, conflict. Each operation audited.
Task lifecycle: discover, claim, transition, block, complete. Audited via OperationalAudit.
Records scoped_write.shadow events with toolName, decision, lockConflict for all governed write operations.
Observes MCP client connections; journals client.observed events with identity assurance and throttle.
MCP request routing: uses mcp-session-id header to look up transport; no request-level correlation ID generated.
GitHub Actions OIDC bounded-read routes; caller supplies requestId for request/response correlation.
GitHub Actions OIDC bounded-write route for stablecoin fast-forward; caller supplies requestId.
Registry V2 schema validation; auditEvents carry unique eventId for registry-level audit trail.

gaps.description: No HTTP request-level correlation ID for MCP tool calls. Individual MCP requests (/mcp POST) do not generate or propagate a per-request correlation ID. The mcp-session-id maps to a transport session but individual tool invocations within that session are not individually traceable.
No HTTP request-level correlation ID for Express web routes (/dashboard, /git/*, /github/*, /login). These routes carry session authentication but no per-request trace ID.

Deploy routes (createGithubDeployRouter) have no request-level or deploy-operation correlation ID. The attestationId exists for the deploy result but no ID correlates the inbound deploy request to its processing.
SSH CA bootstrap and SSH access routes have no request-level correlation ID.
Provisioning routes (runtime executor, Plesk, GovernPilot) have no request-level correlation ID.
Event Journal eventId is not propagated back to the MCP tool response. A tool caller cannot correlate a tool response to the specific events it generated in the journal.
processSequence resets on server restart. There is no persistent sequence across process restarts; correlation across restarts relies only on timestamps and eventId.

GitHub API request IDs (x-github-request-id) are captured in authorizationDiagnostics but not in normal GitHub API calls (src/github/connection.ts, registry.ts). Failed or slow GitHub API calls cannot be correlated with GitHub's support logs.

No end-to-end trace ID spanning MCP request → governed session operation → event journal → response. The governedSessionId provides session-level correlation but not request-level granularity within a session.

Logger (pino) redacts transportSessionId and sessionId, which is correct for security but makes log-level correlation harder. No alternative non-sensitive request correlation ID exists to replace them in logs.

recommendations.description: Add a per-request operationId (UUID) at the MCP /mcp POST handler entry point, propagated through tool execution context to the Event Journal as metadata.
Add an Express middleware generating a requestId for all HTTP routes and attaching it to pino logger child context. This replaces GAP-02/03/04/05 without a second tracing store.
Capture x-github-request-id from all GitHub API responses (not just diagnostics) and include it in log context for GitHub operation correlation.
Add operationId to ALLOWED_METADATA_KEYS for relevant event types so the Event Journal can carry request-level correlation without schema changes.
Accept an optional client-supplied X-Request-ID / X-Correlation-ID header on MCP and Express routes, falling back to server-generated UUID if absent. This enables upstream-to-downstream tracing.

summary.primaryStrength: Governed session lifecycle (governedSessionId) provides strong session-level correlation across all operational memory components — sessions, tasks, locks, checkpoints, events, scoped writes.
summary.primaryWeakness: No per-request/per-operation correlation ID exists. Individual MCP tool calls and HTTP requests within a session are not individually traceable end-to-end through the Event Journal.
